Along California’s state beaches, state and local governments have effectively banned independent surf instructors from earning a living. The outcome of their lawsuits against the government could crack open economic liberty litigation far beyond California’s coastline. 

The new Cato Podcast episode explores why First Amendment may be a sharp tool to defend economic liberty. 

Apple: ow.ly/9fXh50YBvan  
Spotify: ow.ly/P5Oe50YBvao  
Our website: ow.ly/k8xO50YBvap

The SAVE America Act isn’t a silver bullet for Republican electoral success, says Cato’s @stephen_richer. “Issues like gas prices, a potential Iran war, airport security lines, and the cost of living will matter far more in determining control of Congress in November 2026.” 
ow.ly/i63c50YBszE

The Trump administration’s proposed “Golden Dome,” modeled on Israel’s Iron Dome and AMD, rests on a system now showing clear vulnerabilities. The lesson for the US is clear, says Cato’s @GiltnerBen. 

ow.ly/xhai50YBstT

America’s debt problem isn’t a mystery—it’s the result of policies lawmakers refuse to fix, says Cato’s @RominaBoccia. We’re running massive deficits in a strong economy, while the burden shifts to younger Americans and future taxpayers. 

Congress knows the problem. What’s missing is the will to act.

Video

The USPS has lost $5–$10 billion a year for over a decade. Falling mail volumes and high labor costs mean half-measures won’t fix it. Congress should close little-used post offices, reduce delivery frequency, and move towards privatization, says Cato’s @CatoEdwards.

ow.ly/VaMo50YBka9

Not all college closures are a tragedy, says Cato’s @Gillen_Andrew_J. Most closures are in some sense inevitable and do not indicate a system-wide crisis. While painful for current students and staff, closures often protect future students and staff and free up both to pursue more promising paths.
ow.ly/CILh50YBhbo

Prisoners released under the First Step Act have significantly lower recidivism rates. The Bureau of Prisons, however, denies credits to thousands who qualify. Cato's Matthew Cavedon argues the Eighth Circuit should correct the Bureau's error. 
ow.ly/Jj6t50YAVXM

The SAVE America Act isn’t just about voter ID—it hands huge power to an executive branch agency to decide the rules after it becomes law. Vague, rushed, and risky. Congress doesn’t want to tell us how the law will be enforced, and that’s the real problem, warns Cato’s @WalterOlsonMd. cato.org/blog/save-america-a…

Seattle mandated higher per-task pay for app drivers—but tips dropped, unpaid idle time rose, and drivers completed fewer jobs. Those offsets wiped out the gains, leaving monthly earnings unchanged. Price controls on wages do not work, explains Cato's @jeffreyamiron.
ow.ly/Kosk50YAVU4

The DHS shutdown tops 40 days, yet the One Big Beautiful Bill’s $191 billion infusion—7x ICE’s annual budget—keeps operations running. Without public records of allocations and spending, Congress cannot oversee executive actions or protect taxpayer dollars, warns Cato’s @LettDominik. cato.org/blog/heres-how-admi…

In most high-income nations, the government sets the regulatory structure, while airports and private firms conduct security screening. That is needed in the US so air travelers are not held hostage by TSA and dysfunctional federal budgeting, says Cato’s @CatoEdwards cato.org/blog/fixing-airport…

$88 trillion over the next 75 years. That’s the gap between what Washington has promised and what it can pay—driven almost entirely by Social Security and Medicare. 

There is no realistic path to fiscal solvency that avoids reducing spending on the major entitlement programs, says Cato’s @RominaBoccia. 

ow.ly/ibUr50YAOhh

While the FED cannot change foreign policy, it can help mitigate market volatility when supply chains are disrupted. Rules-based monetary policy is not perfect, but it’s predictable and more stable than the status quo, says Cato’s @JaiKedia. 
cato.org/blog/feds-best-resp…

Legal and illegal immigrants have a lower incarceration rate than native-born Americans of the same race or ethnicity, the 2024 data show.  

Learn more in the new study by @AlexNowrasteh and Michelangelo Landgrove, “Illegal Immigrant Incarceration Rates, 2010–2024: The Demographics of American Imprisonment.” 

ow.ly/k7fJ50YyR6y

The solution to America’s deficits isn’t raising taxes. 

There isn’t enough untaxed wealth to close a multi-trillion-dollar deficit, explains Cato's @adamnmichel. 

Controlling spending is the key.  

ow.ly/nGEX50YxEmZ

Or as P. J. O'Rourke put it:

The Cato Institute is pleased to announce that constitutional attorney Molly Nixon is joining the Institute as Senior Fellow in Executive Power. 
cato.org/news-releases/molly…

Spain froze rents and capped increases at 2%, but rent control is already cutting supply by up to 50% and not improving conditions for renters. Spain should follow Argentina, which ended rent control in 2023 and has seen housing supply rise 180%, reports Cato’s @hiperfalcon.
